_comment: ZincAI runtime defaults. Every value can be overridden by environment variables, which is how a PufferPanel template configures it: MC_HOST, MC_PORT, MC_VERSION, MC_AUTH, MC_ALLOW_SCAFFOLDING, MC_AUTO_ELYTRA, AMD_API_BASE_URL, AMD_MODEL, AMD_API_KEY (or API_KEY / RADEON_API_KEY), AMD_MAX_TOKENS, AMD_TEMPERATURE, AMD_API_TIMEOUT_MS, AMD_CHAT_TIMEOUT_MS, AMD_MAX_CONCURRENT, BOT_MODE, BOT_ALIASES, BOT_LANGUAGE, INFERENCE_RPM, INFERENCE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS, INFERENCE_HEARTBEAT_MS, RECONNECT, RECONNECT_MAX_ATTEMPTS, ZINC_DATA_DIR, LOG_LEVEL. Dotted names (server.host, amd.model, ...) are accepted too and mean the same key in this file. There is no .env: leave amd.apiKey EMPTY and let the panel pass the key as a secret variable.

server._note: Built-in defaults only: the panel (MC_HOST / MC_PORT / MC_VERSION / MC_AUTH) always wins. version '' = auto-detect. auth 'offline' joins a private server with the fixed name ZincAI whitelisted; 'microsoft' needs a premium account and an interactive device-code login.

amd._modelNote: Radeon Cloud Token Factory alias for the Qwen 3.8 27B free standing model. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 also works.
amd._timeoutNote: 26.1 live test (2026-11-12): Qwen3.8-27B measured 47-99s per action-lane call (9.7k-token prompts) and hit 256-token cutoffs. Raised maxTokens to 512 and chatTimeoutMs to 90000.
amd._lanesNote: maxConcurrent 2 = the chat lane and the action lane each have one call in flight, so a slow action call never holds a chat reply (set 1 if the endpoint refuses parallel requests; chat still goes first). chatTimeoutMs 90000 accommodates Qwen3.8-27B latency (~47s p50) while remaining shorter than action timeoutMs (120000); adaptive p90 scaling lifts slow calls automatically.

inference._note: Two lanes: chat (reads people) and action (drives the body). Wake-ups are queued, never dropped. rpm is the shared calls-per-minute budget — the API's pacing, which is the only budget that still limits the model; chatReserve of those are for the chat lane alone. chatBatchMs is the IRC window: chat lines are collected this long and handed over as ONE chunk (several speakers, in order) instead of one model call per line; 0 turns batching off. urgentMinIntervalMs: the start of an escape or being cornered may be thought about this soon after the last call. heartbeatMs is the longest the agent loop ever waits between turns when nothing happens (0 = loop off); see _loopNote.
inference._chatBatchNote: chat is delivered in 6 s chunks, IRC-style, and only when there is data: the first line of a quiet stretch opens the window, everything said inside it joins the same chunk. Chat is answered by its own lane WHILE the body works: it does not cancel the action thought. Only a request the chat lane hands to the body (reply.do / reply.task) preempts that thought.
inference._loopNote: THE AGENT LOOP. A turn is think -> call tools -> read their results -> think again, up to maxStepsPerTurn model calls, ending when the model calls idle or puts the body to work. The next turn then starts by itself loopMs after the last one ended (env INFERENCE_LOOP_MS); while the model keeps answering idle the gap doubles up to heartbeatMs, and anything that happens resets it. While the body is busy with a task the loop looks in every loopBusyMs. loopMs 0 or heartbeatMs 0 turns the loop off (events only). timelineMax is how many lines the IRC-style log (chat + events, each with its clock time) keeps.
inference._failGateNote: the same tool call with the same arguments failing failGateAfter times inside failWindowMs is refused locally (no wake) until the world changes (success, movement, hurt, new threat, timeout).

memory._chatRecallNote: Memory recall on non-chat wakes uses the last chat line only while it is this fresh : hours-old chat stopped steering recall into flee/task prompts.

behavior._note: No modes, no friend list, no PvP switch, no language: the model has every tool on every turn and decides for itself what to do, whom to answer and in which language. Its reflex toward a real threat is to flee until it decides otherwise, and what a walk may break on its own is the model's own standing rule (`digging` below, the `dig_policy` tool); anything else it breaks on purpose with `dig`.

digging._note: What a WALK may break on its own. The model owns this at run time through the dig_policy tool (switch, mode, list) and its edits are saved in <data dir>/dig-policy.json, which then wins over these values; these are only the first-run defaults. enabled: the can-dig flag. mode list = only blocks on the list, all = anything except the never-break set (bedrock, portals, spawners...). allow: null = the built-in soft-terrain list (dirt, grass, sand, gravel, snow, leaves; no stone, ore or wood); or your own array of block ids, * is a wildcard. cost: path cost added per broken block, so a route around is preferred when it is short. Whatever the policy says, a walk never breaks a block that touches a crafted block (a build) or lies inside someone's claim, and the operator switch actions.allowDig turns all of it off.

system1._note: Survival reflexes. eatBelowFood: eat under this hunger (never wasting food, except when hurt: then the bar is brought back to 18 so health regenerates). lowHealth: eat a golden apple if carried. fleeBelowHealth: too hurt to honour earlier decisions - flee from everything. mlgFallBlocks: shortest fall worth a water-bucket clutch. FLEEING: an escape starts when a threat is inside threat.radius and lasts while anything still follows inside releaseRadius or keeps closing; it is over after calmMs with nothing following. The model is told at the start, on material changes (at most every reportGapMs unless urgent), every stillFleeingMs while it lasts, and at the end; recallMs is how long the last escape stays in the prompts. fleeDistance is only used by the fallback planner.
system1._tetherNote: With a walk under way (follow, go_to, any errand) an escape is a short DODGE, not a retreat: it starts only when something hostile is inside tetherTriggerRadius, is planned toward where the walk was heading, ends after tetherCalmMs with nothing inside tetherReleaseRadius, and the walk then carries on by itself. At lowHealth or below the full escape applies again. tether false restores the old behaviour.

combat._note: Only ever started by the attack tool. critThreshold is the fraction of the attack indicator required before a swing; vanilla cannot crit below 0.9, so values under 0.9 are raised to 0.9. maxChainKills: how many HOSTILE mobs of the named kind one attack call may take in a row; animals are one per call unless the call gives a count.

threat._note: What counts as a threat (threats.js) and how A* avoids it (PredictiveThreatMap): every path step pays for coming near a hostile - inside its standoff ring (creeper 7 blocks, shooters 8, melee 5; standoffScale multiplies the table, standoff:false switches the ring off), at the spot it will reach in two seconds, and on its line to the bot. A route already being walked is planned AGAIN when a mob moves onto it: routeReplanCost is how costly a step ahead must have become, routeReplanRise how much worse than when the route was planned, routeReplanMs the least time between two re-plans (0 = never re-plan). radius/rangedRadius: the trigger ring - how close a hostile mob (melee / ranged) must be to start an escape. Further out, up to 32 blocks, hostiles in the open are watched: counted for the model and used to decide when an escape is over. attackerMemoryMs: how long something that hit the bot stays a threat. Players are never threats unless they hit the bot.

traversal._note: Wind-charge traversal. Used only when A* reports noPath across a 3-5 wide gap or <=4 high wall.

scout._note: Optional startup Scout & Relocate (walks to the safest nearby anchor). OFF by default: the bot now stays where it spawns (its bed) and the flee reflex handles danger.

reconnect._note: After a session that had spawned successfully, reconnect with back-off when the server restarts or the link drops. A rejection on the FIRST join (whitelist, name) is still fatal: no retries, no renames.

goals._note: Durable objectives (goals.js). Every long task becomes a record with an id, origin, priority, checkpoint and lifecycle; it survives deaths, restarts and context resets (goals.json in the data dir). stallMs: an ACTIVE goal whose checkpoint has not moved for this long wakes the model once (remindMs before a second nudge) — waiting on a furnace or the night is legitimate, so only the running goal is nudged and never failed automatically. maxFails: repeated failures plus no progress suspend it as blocked. starveMs/starveRemindMs: an open goal that waits this long while the body is idle is offered back to the model. maxResumes: a main task paused this many times is set aside (not deleted). verifyRadius: a restored build goal within this many blocks of its site is re-checked at startup (farther away it is left resumable+needsVerify; gather goals are always checked, they have no site). staleGuard: refuse quiet actions whose snapshot no longer matches the world (new threat or a different active goal).

places._note: Place memory: chests, furnaces, beds, signs seen while walking, plus named places. Stored in zincai-data/places.json. A storage room (more containers than fit on one prompt line) is shown as a summary with every label.

identity._note: Optional operator-supplied creator identity. A UUID match alone is not proof of authentication on offline-mode or proxy servers. Never use a name or appearance as proof.
